facts.one_liner: A Georgian naval dockyard and, legend says, 365 beaches.
facts.why_go: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year. Nelson’s Dockyard in English Harbour, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a restored Georgian naval base that now hosts yachts and the famous Antigua Sailing Week. Shirley Heights lookout gives views over English and Falmouth harbours, especially at sunset.
facts.how_to_get_there: V.C. Bird International Airport has flights from North America and Europe.
facts.good_to_know: Sunday sunset parties at Shirley Heights are popular.

facts.one_liner: A chic Caribbean island with red-roofed Gustavia and white beaches.
facts.why_go: Saint Barthélemy, or St. Barths, is a small French island in the Caribbean known for its chic style. The red-roofed capital, Gustavia, named during a period of Swedish rule, wraps around a harbour full of yachts. Beaches such as Saline, Gouverneur and Shell Beach are among the most beautiful in the region.
facts.how_to_get_there: Short flights from Saint Martin.
facts.good_to_know: The airport runway is very short.

facts.one_liner: Willemstad’s pastel Dutch waterfront and reef-fringed coves.
facts.why_go: Curaçao’s capital, Willemstad, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site where pastel-coloured Dutch colonial buildings line the Handelskade waterfront, linked by the floating Queen Emma Bridge. Beyond town, the island has dozens of small coves with clear water and coral reefs, and it lies outside the main hurricane belt.
facts.best_time: Year-round; it is outside the main hurricane belt.
facts.how_to_get_there: Curaçao International Airport has flights from the Americas and Europe.
facts.good_to_know: Rent a car to reach western beaches.

facts.one_liner: A diver’s paradise of protected reefs and salt flats.
facts.why_go: Bonaire is one of the world’s top shore-diving destinations: the waters around the island are protected as Bonaire National Marine Park, and reefs start just metres from shore. Kralendijk is a small, colourful capital with Fort Oranje on the waterfront. Flamingos feed in the salt pans of the south, and Washington Slagbaai National Park covers the wild north.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flamingo International Airport has flights from the Americas and Europe.
facts.good_to_know: A nature fee is required.

facts.one_liner: Caribbean reefs on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.
facts.why_go: Roatán is the largest of Honduras’s Bay Islands and lies on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second-largest barrier reef in the world. Its clear water makes it one of the most affordable places in the Caribbean to learn to dive. West End and West Bay are the main beach areas, and the island has a mix of English-speaking and Garifuna communities.
facts.how_to_get_there: Juan Manuel Gálvez International Airport; ferries from La Ceiba.
facts.good_to_know: Check reef-safe sunscreen rules.

facts.one_liner: Belize’s largest island, near the barrier reef and Hol Chan.
facts.why_go: Ambergris Caye is Belize’s largest island, close to the Belize Barrier Reef, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Snorkel trips visit Hol Chan Marine Reserve and Shark Ray Alley, where nurse sharks and stingrays gather. San Pedro is the main town, and golf carts are the usual way to get around. Secret Beach on the lagoon side has shallow turquoise water.
facts.how_to_get_there: Short flights or water taxis from Belize City.
facts.good_to_know: Golf carts are a common way to get around.

facts.one_liner: Stilt houses and UNESCO wooden churches on a misty island.
facts.why_go: Chiloé, off the coast of southern Chile, has a culture all its own. In Castro, colourful palafitos—stilt houses—stand over the water, and sixteen wooden churches built by Jesuit missionaries and local carpenters are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The island is rich in myths and known for curanto, a seafood and meat dish cooked in an earth pit.
facts.how_to_get_there: Ferries cross the Chacao Channel from Pargua; flights to Castro.
facts.good_to_know: Rain is common—bring waterproofs.

facts.one_liner: A car-free rainforest island with clear lagoons.
facts.why_go: Ilha Grande, off the coast between Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, is covered in Atlantic Forest and has no cars. Trails link the village of Abraão to beaches such as Lopes Mendes, and boat trips visit Lagoa Azul, a natural pool of clear water between the island and a smaller islet. The island was once a prison, which helped preserve its nature.
facts.how_to_get_there: Boats from Angra dos Reis and Conceição de Jacareí.
facts.good_to_know: There are no cars—bring light luggage.

facts.one_liner: Long beaches and a national park lighthouse on Thailand’s Andaman coast.
facts.why_go: Koh Lanta is a laid-back island in Thailand’s Andaman Sea with long sandy beaches on its west coast. At its southern tip, Mu Ko Lanta National Park has a lighthouse on a headland and forest trails. Lanta Old Town on the east coast has wooden stilt houses built by Chinese traders and Sea Gypsy (Chao Leh) communities.
facts.how_to_get_there: Ferries and vans from Krabi.
facts.good_to_know: Many places close in the rainy season.

facts.one_liner: Three islets joined by a sandbar off Koh Tao.
facts.why_go: Koh Nang Yuan is a group of three small islands off Koh Tao, joined by a sandbar that creates a beach between two seas. A short climb leads to a viewpoint looking down on the sandbar and the turquoise reef. The surrounding waters are good for snorkelling and diving.
facts.how_to_get_there: Boats from Koh Tao’s Mae Haad pier take about 15 minutes.
facts.good_to_know: An entry fee applies; plastic bottles are not allowed.

facts.one_liner: George Town’s shophouses, temples and street food.
facts.why_go: Penang is a Malaysian island whose capital, George Town, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with shophouses, Chinese clan houses, mosques and temples. The city is famous for street food, from char kway teow to assam laksa, and for street art. Penang Hill offers views over the city and strait.
facts.how_to_get_there: Penang International Airport; bridges from the mainland.
facts.good_to_know: Hawker centres are busy in the evenings.

facts.one_liner: Coconut palms and Cloud 9 surf.
facts.why_go: Siargao, in the south-east Philippines, is known for Cloud 9, one of the world’s best surf breaks. Inland, coconut palms stretch for miles, and boat trips visit Naked Island, Daku and Guyam islands, and the Sugba Lagoon.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights to Sayak Airport.
facts.good_to_know: Rent a scooter to get around.

facts.one_liner: The Chocolate Hills and tiny tarsiers.
facts.why_go: Bohol is famous for the Chocolate Hills, more than 1,200 grass-covered limestone mounds that turn brown in the dry season. The island is also home to the tarsier, one of the world’s smallest primates, as well as old Spanish churches, river cruises and Panglao Island’s beaches.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights to Panglao; ferries from Cebu.
facts.good_to_know: Visit tarsiers at responsible sanctuaries.

facts.one_liner: Limestone cliffs, clear lakes and WWII shipwrecks.
facts.why_go: Coron, in northern Palawan, is a world of limestone cliffs and clear lakes. Kayangan Lake and Barracuda Lake are reached by boat and short climbs, and Japanese shipwrecks from a 1944 air raid make it one of the world’s top wreck-diving sites.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights to Busuanga; ferries from Manila and El Nido.
facts.good_to_know: Island-hopping requires fees.

facts.one_liner: Kerama-blue water and white beaches near Okinawa.
facts.why_go: Zamami is one of the Kerama Islands, part of Keramashotō National Park west of Okinawa. Its beaches, such as Furuzamami and Ama, have white sand and very clear water known as ‘Kerama blue’. Humpback whales visit in winter, and sea turtles are often seen near shore.
facts.how_to_get_there: Ferries from Naha’s Tomari Port.
facts.good_to_know: Book ferries ahead.

facts.one_liner: Kabira Bay’s turquoise water and coral reefs.
facts.why_go: Ishigaki is the main island of the Yaeyama Islands in Japan’s far south-west. Kabira Bay is known for its colours, and glass-bottom boats show the coral beneath. The island is also a gateway to Taketomi and Iriomote islands.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights from Tokyo, Osaka and Naha.
facts.good_to_know: Swimming is prohibited in Kabira Bay.

facts.one_liner: Three car-free islands with turtles and beach bars.
facts.why_go: Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno and Gili Air are three small coral islands off Lombok with no motor vehicles. Gili Trawangan is the liveliest, Gili Meno the quietest, and Gili Air somewhere in between. Snorkellers often see sea turtles.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fast boats from Bali or boats from Bangsal on Lombok.
facts.good_to_know: Get around by bicycle or on foot.

facts.one_liner: Karst islands and the world’s richest coral reefs.
facts.why_go: Raja Ampat, off the western tip of New Guinea, has the highest recorded marine biodiversity on Earth, with hundreds of coral species and more than a thousand types of reef fish. The viewpoint at Piaynemo looks over a maze of karst islands rising from turquoise lagoons.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Sorong, then ferry to Waisai.
facts.good_to_know: A marine park permit is required.

facts.one_liner: A turquoise lagoon dotted with islets.
facts.why_go: Aitutaki is an almost-atoll with a lagoon of turquoise water scattered with small islets. Lagoon cruises visit One Foot Island (Tapuaetai), where you can get a passport stamp, and snorkelling sites with giant clams.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights from Rarotonga take about 50 minutes.
facts.good_to_know: Respect local customs.

facts.one_liner: Twin peaks over the world’s southernmost coral reef.
facts.why_go: Lord Howe Island, about 600 km off the coast of New South Wales, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The peaks of Mount Gower and Mount Lidgbird rise above a lagoon with the world’s southernmost coral reef. Visitor numbers are capped, so the island stays quiet.
facts.how_to_get_there: Flights from Sydney, Brisbane or Port Macquarie.
facts.good_to_know: Accommodation must be booked before travel.
